observation.visible_scene: First-person (POV) view from a whitewater kayaker descending a granite-boulder rapid. A bright pink kayak bow bearing a Red Bull logo sits at the bottom center of frame throughout. The kayaker, in a yellow/black drysuit with a watch on the left wrist, holds a black Werner paddle with pink grip tape. Churning white water fills the channel between smooth rock walls under a clear blue sky; sun glare and water droplets on the lens appear later.
visible_changes: Frames 1-10: The paddle is held with the left hand high on the pink shaft and the right hand low; the black blade is mostly out of view, then rotates into frame at the top as the stroke turns, sweeping from upper-right toward center.
Frames 11-18: The paddle continues its arc; the black blade (Werner logo visible) swings up and to the left side of frame, then lowers, while the bow stays pointed forward into the rapids.
Frames 19-22: The paddle drops mostly out of frame; the camera tilts upward, enlarging the sky and the overhanging rock on the right, with heavy spray crossing the lens.

Frames 23-41: The paddle is carried low and roughly horizontal across the bow, right hand near the blade on the right side; the kayak translates forward down the chute toward a narrowing rock gap, and the background boulders shift leftward/downward relative to the frame as the kayak advances.
Throughout: Water spray and lens droplets progressively accumulate, and a sun flare/lens reflection grows in the upper-right from about frame 33 onward.
outside_clip_unknowns: The maneuver that preceded the high left-hand grip at t=0 and the outcome after t=1.33 (whether the kayak clears the rapid, stops, or capsizes) are not shown.
The exact stroke type (forward, brace, or draw) and whether the kayak is on a drop or flat water cannot be confirmed from this excerpt.
uncertain_details: Camera motion (tilt/roll) and the kayak's own pitch/roll are coupled and cannot be fully separated; apparent background movement reflects both forward translation and body/camera rotation.
Droplets on the lens and the rainbow-colored flare are reflections/spray on the camera, not separate objects in the scene.
The paddle blade's leftward sweep in frames 11-18 is the kayaker's arm motion, not the kayak turning; the bow heading remains broadly forward.
